articles.title: Professional chefs reveal the go-to ingredients they always keep in their fridge and pantry
articles.summary: These home kitchen provisions will enhance even the simplest and speediest of meals.
articles.body:
Our experts independently review everything we recommend. If you buy through our links, we may earn commission.

I'm an admittedly nosy person, especially when it comes to food. I love a good "grocery haul" video on TikTok, and whenever I walk past outdoor seating at a restaurant, I like to scope out the meals on everyone's tables. Of course, I'm extra curious about what culinary professionals eat; as a former full-time baker, I know that most people who choose to work in an industrial kitchen take food seriously.

That's why I asked five chefs to dish about the fridge and pantry items they always have at home. From condiments and seasonings to produce and dry goods, these are the building blocks they use to whip up fantastic food, even while they're off the clock. (Spoiler alert: Even chefs appreciate a good shortcut, and there's no shame in store-bought sundries!) I know what I'll be adding to my shopping list, and maybe you'll take some inspiration for your next grocery run too.

Chefs, they're just like us! Well, when it comes to refrigerator requisites, that is. Alex Carballo, chef and partner of Grand Restaurant Group in Southern California, and Peter Ki Suk Tondreau, chef and co-owner/operator of LenLen in New York City, count eggs among their must-haves, and both Tondreau and Matt Sramek, regional executive chef of Southern California's Urban Kitchen Group , are never without some good ol' butter. (Tondreau specifies that he opts for unsalted European-style butter, which I also recommend for baking due to its higher fat content.)

Because of its high fat content, butter is prone to absorbing odors around it, which can alter its taste in not-so-pleasant ways. This highly-rated keeper has an airtight lid, as well as small "ramps" at each end, which make it easier to scoop up a pat.

"Chick" this out: This egg holder has slots for 14 eggs and a lid so you can stack other items on top to make better use of the room in your fridge. Not only is its clear design more aesthetically pleasing than a cardboard carton, but it also lets you see your egg inventory. See? You can count your chickens before they're hatched.

Dominique Leach, chef and owner of Lexington Betty Smokehouse in Chicago, stocks up on a mix of store-bought and homemade items, proving even chefs don't feel the need to make everything from scratch. For instance, she's a fan of Aldi's Classic Chicken Salad "because it's basic and makes for a super easy lunch on the go." Another pre-made favorite? Caruso Provisions' giardiniera , which "is good for elevating anything, but amazing on a brisket Italian beef." That said, a "super versatile" homemade chipotle aioli is one of her go-tos, because it's "good on everything."

When it comes to homemade condiments and leftovers, I like to keep them in glass jars like these. The airtight lids help prevent spoilage and spillage, and if I'm storing something like salad dressing, I can easily give it a shake. Plus, the jars are easy to stack and dishwasher-safe.

Of course, they wouldn't be chefs if they didn't have some "cheffier" provisions on hand. Tondreau and Accursio Lota, chef/owner of Dora Ristorante in La Jolla, CA, keep fancy blocks of Parmigiano Reggiano in the fridge, and on the condiment front, Tondreau is a fan of chili pastes like "gochujang, Calabrian chili or sambal," as well as fermented citrus. "Quality fats carry aromatics, while sharp acids (citrus, vinegars) cut through richness and brighten dull flavors right before serving," he explains.

Sure, you could grate cheese using a standard box grater, but having one of these on hand allows you to shave parm right over your food. And it's not just a cheese grater; when I was baking professionally, I'd sometimes have to zest dozens of lemons a day, and this rasp was a game-changer when it came to getting the job done quickly, effectively and safely. (I can't tell you how many times I've nicked myself trying to zest citrus using a box grater, but since this is handheld, it offers much more control.)

I might not be zesting quite as much these days, but I'm still grateful for this gadget every time I'm faced with the task. It earns its keep by grating cheese, chocolate, ginger and garlic, or even spices like nutmeg. The brand also recommends using it to shave corks down to fit back into wine bottles or scraping away burnt spots on toast. Who knew?

The pantry is where you can really go wild, since items stored there typically have long shelf lives. While the chefs I spoke to had extensive lists of pantry standbys, cooking oils were by far the most commonly mentioned ingredients. Lota, Sramek and Tondreau all included extra-virgin olive oil , while Sramek added that he reaches for "avocado oil for high-heat cooking." Tondreau also relies on "neutral cooking fats," like avocado and grapeseed oils, which won't add strong flavors to food.

Vinegar was another popular inclusion; Sramek keeps "various vinegars" at the ready, while Tondreau specifically calls out unseasoned rice vinegar, in addition to "fermented or aged umami builders," like soy sauce, fish sauce, Shaoxing wine, dry white wine and "high-quality tomato paste in a tube." (Raise your hand if you've ever purchased a can of tomato paste and only needed a few tablespoons for a recipe — tubes make leftover storage so much easier.) Plus, according to Tondreau, these ingredients "hold up for months in the fridge or pantry, turning pantry grain or noodle bases into balanced meals on short notice."

This item has single-handedly changed the way I cook with oil — my husband and I reach for it nightly. Before I purchased it, I would use an olive oil spout attached to the bottle to coat my pans in oil — too much oil. Now, I can spritz just a light layer to keep things flavorful without excess grease. Unlike the oil misters my mom used in the '90s, this one has never clogged, and you don't need to pump it. Plus, I think it looks really nice on my counter.

Any chef worth their salt knows that properly seasoning food is important — and speaking of salt, both Sramek and Tondreau prefer Diamond Crystal kosher salt . Kosher salt flakes are larger than tiny table salt granules, which makes them ideal for sprinkling over food with more control. Tondreau also opts for "whole black peppercorns in a mill" versus powdery pre-ground pepper.

If you're ready to try your hand at pepper grinding, which can impart a fresher flavor than using pre-ground peppercorns, this affordable model made it to our list of the best pepper mills we tried. "An electric pepper grinder can be quite helpful to anyone with arthritis or hand-strength issues," says our tester. "This large model from Eparé is 8.74" tall and has a capacity of 2 ounces, which is at the top end of most pepper mills."

"Once you follow the included instructions for filling the reservoir and installing the batteries, you place the top back on and turn it using the arrows as a guide. Then you simply press the round button on top to activate the grinder. An LED illuminates the pepper as it grinds, allowing you to clearly see how much comes out and how coarse it is. To adjust the level of coarseness, turn the dial on the bottom of the mill — it's very easy to do. A plastic end cap is also included for mess-free storage. Overall, this gadget is a total steal for $25."

In addition to salt, Carballo says that his pantry is always stocked with flour and sugar. "There's nothing worse than starting a recipe and realizing you're missing the basics," he shares, adding that with his top essentials, "you can create so many different things, and they all have a long shelf life and are used together frequently."

Pasta di grano (or, pasta made simply with grain and water), along with salted anchovies, are mainstays in Lota's pantry. "These are basic ingredients I use every day, and they allow me to cook very good food, especially when I'm short on time with three young kids," he says.

To help prevent pest attraction, it's wise to store dry goods like flour, sugar and pasta in airtight food storage containers rather than the paper packaging they often come in. Thousands of shoppers praise this attractive set for its leak-resistant bamboo lids and stackable design. "I absolutely love these!" exclaimed a fan . "I use them for my pantry to hold my flour, nuts, baking powder, etc. and they are airtight and look very nice. I like how organized it makes my pantry look."

If you enjoy preparing pasta, having a large stockpot like this will really come in handy. It's tall enough to accommodate shapes long and short, and its sturdy stainless steel and aluminum construction makes it an excellent heat conductor and distributor. The glass lid allows you to keep an eye on your food as it cooks, and without the lid, the pot can go into ovens of up to 500° F.

Some fruits and vegetables — especially those that have been cut up — need to be stored in the fridge, while others can be kept at room temperature for a long time. Among the latter are fresh lemons and limes, onions and garlic, which Sramek stocks up on. "I like balance and acidity in my food, and onions and garlic are a great base to start any recipe," he explains.

Tondreau keeps similar ingredients at the ready; his picks include "aromatics and umami bases" like fresh garlic, whole shallots, ginger knobs and dried shiitake and porcini mushrooms. He notes that combining these with his aforementioned condiment staples "allows you to build deep flavor in under twenty minutes without relying on long-simmered stocks." Meals that are speedy and delicious? Yes, please!

I love cooking with onions, but chopping them? That's another story. If you're like me (meaning, your eyes feel like they've been stung by a hundred jellyfish every time you slice an allium), this wildly popular gizmo will become one of your most-reached-for tools. It chops veggies into tiny, uniform pieces with just one push, and because everything falls into the attached tray, you'll keep your counter clean too.

The reviews quoted above reflect the most recent versions at the time of publication.

articles.title: Veja como foi o dia dos candidatos ao governo do TO nesta sexta-feira | G1
articles.standfirst: Confira as atividades de campanha de Vicentinho Júnior (PSDB) e Du Pereira (DC) nesta sexta-feira (18).
articles.summary: Confira as atividades de campanha de Vicentinho Júnior (PSDB) e Du Pereira (DC).
articles.body:
Confira como foi a agenda de campanha dos candidatos ao governo do Tocantins nesta sexta-feira (18). Professora Dorinha (União) não teve agenda pública durante o dia. Segundo a assessoria da candidata, à noite, ela participou de uma reunião em Arraias, na região sul do estado.

Vicentinho Júnior (PSDB) cumpriu agenda de campanha na capital. Du Pereira (DC) foi o único entre os candidatos com menos de 1% das intenções de voto a ter agenda pública e também passou o dia em Palmas .

Seguindo os critérios da TV Anhanguera , definidos em conjunto com representantes dos partidos e coligações, os candidatos que aparecem com 15% ou mais das intenções de voto na última pesquisa Quaest têm espaço às segundas, quartas e sextas-feiras. Já aqueles com menos de 1% participam da cobertura uma vez a cada 15 dias.

📱 Clique aqui para seguir o canal do g1 TO no WhatsApp

O candidato ao governo pelo PSDB chegou no fim da manhã à sede do partido, em Palmas. Vicentinho esteve com aliados e apoiadores e, em seguida, se reuniu com representantes de federações esportivas do estado. Durante o encontro, os dirigentes entregaram uma carta com propostas para o esporte tocantinense. O documento reúne sugestões que vão desde o incentivo às categorias de base até investimentos em campeonatos e eventos esportivos.

"O esporte no Tocantins não é vivido só em Palmas. Eu falo da minha pesca esportiva, eu tenho condição de fazê-la em vários rios e lagos no meu estado do Tocantins. Eu vi aqui um mestre da minha capoeira, eu sou aluno de mestre Gamela e mestre Michel, da minha Porto Nacional. Então, o esporte se faz vívido em todo o meu estado do Tocantins", Disse o candidato.

Pela manhã, o candidato do Democracia Cristã visitou o comércio do Jardim Aureny III, em Palmas. Ele defendeu uma maior valorização da região.

"Então, aqui nós temos umas propostas amplas. A primeira dela é o acompanhamento dos nossos pequenos empresários, redução dos impostos aqui para as empresas, não só da nossa localidade da região Sul, mas a também a diminuição dos impostos para o nosso estado do Tocantins e o incentivo para os nossos comerciantes", disse candidato.

Du Pereira (DC) e Vicentinho Júnior (PSDB) — Foto: Reprodução/TV Anhanguera

A frequência da cobertura segue o desempenho de cada candidato na pesquisa Quaest mais recente , conforme acordo firmado com representantes dos partidos e coligações.

Candidatos que registraram 15% ou mais das intenções de voto terão a agenda exibida nas segundas, quartas e sexta-feiras. Para aqueles que aparecem com 5% a 14% a cobertura será nas terças e quinta-feiras. Para quem tem menos de 5% será uma vez por semana. Candidatos que não pontuaram (menos de 1%), será uma vez a cada 15 dias.

articles.body:
O g1 , maior portal de notícias do Brasil, completa nesta sexta-feira (18) 20 anos.

Antes de você receber uma notícia do g1 , essa informação passou por um processo super-rigoroso de apuração, para garantir que ela esteja 100% correta e chegue o mais rápido possível a você. Isso, claro, sempre de acordo com os Princípios Editoriais do Grupo Globo - seja em um post de rede social, em um vídeo ou em uma notícia no nosso site.

A notícia pode acontecer em qualquer lugar porque a gente tem redação no interior do Brasil. Em São Paulo tem, inclusive, uma equipe que cuida exatamente disso, do que cada afiliada está fazendo.

Luiza Tenente, repórter do g1: Vou conversar até com o Cau, que cuida dessa parte, está coordenando essa força-tarefa. Cau, com quem você está falando agora? Cau Rodrigues, editor do g1: Oi, Luiza. Agora, eu estou falando com o Mato Grosso, mas não para, não. O país todo aqui chamando a equipe o tempo inteiro para discutir o que está acontecendo por aí. Luiza Tenente: É isso mesmo, gente. Eu sento aqui perto e eu escuto: é telefone, mensagem o dia inteiro.

O pessoal de Internacional também está de olho nas agências de notícia do mundo inteiro e em todas as informações enviadas pelos correspondentes.

Luiza Tenente: Opa, minha xará. Luísa, tudo bem? Estou fazendo um vídeo de bastidores do g1 . Vocês aqui de Internacional, o que vocês precisam cobrir em um mesmo dia? O que pode ocorrer ao redor do mundo na mesma data e vocês podem dar conta de tudo? Luisa Belchior, editora g1: Nosso leque é muito amplo. Desde um terremoto de uma magnitude importante, que a gente tenha que parar e olhar, um novo conflito, ou uma declaração de paz, de um acordo de paz. Então, o leque é bastante amplo, e a gente fica muito ligado para não perder nada.

g1, o maior portal de notícias do Brasil, completa 20 anos — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

E a gente não só noticia o que aconteceu, a gente explica por quê, dá um contexto, se aprofunda. E quando você tem repórteres especialistas em cada assunto, essas explicações ficam muito mais completas. É assim que a cobertura ganha em qualidade e em aprofundamento. Tudo vai acontecendo de forma simultânea.

Enquanto um jornalista está analisando mais profundamente o tema e fazendo entrevistas, outro já checa se as imagens são verdadeiras, o pessoal de redes dispara os posts, a equipe que cuida da página inicial do g1 troca manchete, manda notificações. Quem é de vídeos já vai escrevendo o roteiro, os designers montam os infográficos... A redação não para.

“O lema mais forte do g1 é a confiança que o público tem na gente. O público confia que a gente consegue fazer um jornalismo sério, um jornalismo com rigor de apuração, com escolhas de temas que são relevantes para o público, que são relevantes para todos eles, e que a gente consegue fazer isso consistentemente”, afirma Renato Franzini, diretor do g1.

Por isso que o g1 consegue levar informação correta de maneira tão ágil e em tantos formatos diferentes. Algo que aconteça de manhã já se torna o assunto no podcast; vira reportagem escrita no site; o vídeo vertical é compartilhado nas redes, aparece no g1 em 1 Minuto na TV, no Jornal Nacional no QR Code. Nesses 20 anos, a gente inovou muito. Mas o que não mudou foi o cuidado com a informação.

articles.title: Show de Fiuk faz fã encarar ônibus de BH para Campinas e atrai até cover de Fabio Jr  | G1
articles.standfirst: Show na noite desta sexta-feira (18) atraiu fãs de várias regiões, uma admiradora que saiu de Belo Horizonte e até um cover de Fábio Jr.
articles.summary: Show na noite desta sexta-feira (18) atraiu fãs de várias regiões, uma admiradora que saiu de Belo Horizonte e até um cover de Fábio Jr., todos na expectativa de que a pausa não se
articles.body:
Tratado como o último show de Fiuk antes de uma pausa na carreira , a apresentação em Campinas (SP), nesta sexta-feira (18), atraiu público de diferentes regiões do estado de São Paulo e até uma fã que encarou uma viagem de ônibus de Belo Horizonte (MG) para ver o artista.

Para completar, na plateia à espera do artista estava até um cover de Fabio Jr. Embora a relação familiar verdadeira esteja estremecida, o sósia previa que a noite não seria um ponto final da carreira de Fiuk .

"Espero que esse show seja o primeiro de muitos que virão pelo Brasil todo", disse Flávio Junior, de 64 anos.

Mas foi o temor de não ver mais o artista nos palcos que fez Sandra Araújo dos Santos, de 39 anos, percorrer mais de 500 quilômetros de estrada.

"Fui ao show 12 anos atrás, e cansei de esperar por ele por lá. Agora eu que vou atrás onde ele estiver", brincou.

Sandra saiu da capital mineira com destino a Campinas, e chegou próximo ao horário do show.

"Foi em cima da hora. Vou embora amanhã mesmo. É a realização de um sonho. Espero que não seja o último show", disse.

Quem também se deslocou a Campinas para ver o cantor pela primeira vez nos palcos foi Renan Lima, de 27 anos.

Morador de Bragança Paulista (SP), ele se surpreendeu quando, ao entrar no local do show ainda vazio, se deparou com a banda Hori passando o som.

"No momento que entrei, começou a tocar minha música predileta. Foi um momento sublime, já valeu a pena", afirmou.

Cover de Fabio Jr. e fãs de Belo Horizonte (MG) e Bragança Paulista (SP) marcaram presença no show de Fiuk em Campinas (SP), nesta sexta-feira (18) — Foto: Bárbara Camilotti

Começo na Hori, sucesso em 'Malhação' e filme não lançado

Filipe Kartalian Ayres Galvão, o Fiuk, começou a projetar o próprio nome no meio musical nos anos 2000 à frente da banda de pop rock Hori.

O alcance do grupo se multiplicou em 2009, quando o cantor assumiu o protagonismo da temporada de "Malhação" na TV Globo no papel do estudante Bernardo.

​Em 2011, o cantor consolidou a transição para a carreira solo com o lançamento do álbum "Sou Eu". O disco de estreia marcou o fim das atividades com a Hori e apostou em um pop romântico com forte aceno ao R&B, distanciando o som da pegada roqueira dos primeiros anos.

Em 2026, Fiuk retomou os lançamentos musicais com o EP "M, Vol. 2" e passou a se apresentar com o projeto Fiuk III, que reúne também integrantes que fizeram parte da Hori.

Nos últimos meses, Fiuk tem falado publicamente sobre dificuldades financeiras e familiares.

O cantor havia decidido voltar aos palcos em 2026, mas também vinha tentando retomar um antigo sonho: produzir e protagonizar um filme sobre o universo dos carros.

O projeto, inicialmente divulgado como “Descontrole”, nunca chegou a ser lançado e acabou no centro de uma disputa judicial .

Fiuk sobe ao palco para o show em Campinas (SP), nesta sexta-feira (18), antes da anunciada pausa na carreira como cantor solo — Foto: Bárbara Camilotti

articles.title: Entram em vigor regras para ampliação de data centers no Brasil; veja vantagens e riscos desse mercado na era da IA | G1
articles.standfirst: São bilhões de dólares para construir e equipar um data center, e o setor diz que aliviar os impostos diminui bem esse custo.
articles.summary: São bilhões de dólares para construir e equipar um data center, e o setor diz que aliviar os impostos diminui bem esse custo.
articles.body:
Entrou em vigor a lei que concede incentivos fiscais para empresas instalarem ou ampliarem centros de processamento de dados no Brasil.

Para o ambiente virtual existir, é preciso uma obra de engenharia bem concreta: um data center.

“Qualquer vídeo a que a gente assista, quando a gente faz uma transação via PIX, por exemplo, no segmento financeiro, é porque tem um data center como esse sustentando toda essa operação”, afirma Marcos Siqueira, vice-presidente de empresa de data center.

São prédios onde ninguém mora, mas que guardam dados de praticamente todo mundo. No caso de nós, brasileiros, muitas informações estão em data centers fora do país, porque aqui faltam centros de processamento que deem conta de toda a demanda.

São bilhões de dólares para construir e equipar um data center, e o setor diz que aliviar os impostos diminui bem esse custo. O Regime Especial de Tributação para Serviços de Data Center , o Redata , suspende a cobrança do Imposto de Importação, do PIS/Cofins e do IPI na compra de componentes eletrônicos e bens de tecnologia da informação e comunicação.

Entram em vigor regras para ampliação de data centers no Brasil; veja vantagens e riscos desse mercado na era da IA — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

Segundo cálculos do setor, a estrutura de um data center padrão de IA custa, em média, US$ 1 bilhão. Os equipamentos são a parte mais cara: US$ 4 bilhões a US$ 5 bilhões. O benefício fiscal é aplicado nessa fase.

“É 26% mais caro instalar um data center no Brasil do que um investimento do mesmo porte nos Estados Unidos. Com a aprovação do Redata, essa desvantagem cai para 17%”, afirma Tatiana Ribeiro, diretora-executiva do Movimento Brasil Competitivo.

O Brasil tem cerca de 200 data centers. A inteligência artificial trouxe a necessidade de novos centros. O data center padrão de IA pode consumir 15 vezes mais energia do que outros centros processadores do mesmo tamanho.

A nova lei determina que as empresas devem usar energia de fonte renovável ou de baixa emissão. Entre as contrapartidas, 10% do serviço do data center devem ser destinados ao mercado interno. O setor avalia que o Brasil tem duas vantagens: uma matriz elétrica renovável e tecnologia para usar pouca água.

“Foi adotado como tecnologia padrão, o sistema de refrigeração de circuito fechado, que funciona como um motor de carro. Então, eu não consumo água no data center. Essa tecnologia no Brasil responde por mais de 90% a 95% de todos os data centers já construídos, e todos os novos trabalham com circuito fechado. O Redata vai atrair novos investimentos. E a gente tem a possibilidade de, até 2030, quadruplicar ou quintuplicar o parque instalado de data centers no Brasil, que hoje é em torno de 1 gigawatt de carga de TI instalada”, explica Luís Tossi, vice-presidente da Associação Brasileira de Data Center.

articles.title: Clariana Barão, candidata do Democracia Cristã à Presidência, faz campanha em Pernambuco | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidata disse que pretende investir na Região Nordeste e incentivar o empreendedorismo como forma de gerar riqueza para o país.
articles.summary: Candidata disse que pretende investir na Região Nordeste e incentivar o empreendedorismo como forma de gerar riqueza para o país.
articles.body:
Clariana Barão , candidata do Democracia Cristã , fez campanha no Agreste de Pernambuco.

Clariana Barão visitou a Feira de Artesanatos e de Confecções, um dos pontos turísticos e de comércio de Caruaru. A candidata circulou pelo local. Ela disse que pretende investir na Região Nordeste e incentivar o empreendedorismo como forma de gerar riqueza para o país:

“O nosso governo vai ser diferente. Nós vamos enxugar a despesa, essa despesa tão alta que o governo faz, e nós vamos incentivar o empreendedor. Nós vamos criar linhas de crédito que sejam acessíveis para que ele possa expandir as suas operações. Com isso, a gente gera mais riqueza, mais renda e mais postos de trabalho qualificados”.

articles.title: Tech layoffs tracker 2026: All the job losses across Oracle, Uber, Apple, TikTok, Meta, Microsoft and others
articles.summary: We're more than half way through the year, and there have already been more than 185,000 layoffs across the tech industry — here's what we know.
articles.body:
We've only got a few months left in 2026, but unfortunately we didn't get here without a ton of tech layoffs. In June, 14,000 job cuts happened at EV automaker Lucid, game developer Bungie, trading platform company Robinhood and others. And not too long ago, Microsoft had its latest round of layoffs , affecting 4,800 jobs — mostly across its Xbox gaming division. Shortly after, companies including Samsung, Amazon, Uber and Monday.com followed suit.

According to many reports , the U.S. is at the center of these job cuts. Oracle has had the biggest impact on layoffs this year so far. The annual financial disclosure the company filed on June 23 showed the software giant cut 21,000 jobs over the past year, roughly 13% of its workforce.

"The adoption and deployment of AI technologies across our operations have resulted, and may continue to result, in reductions to our workforce," Oracle said in the filing.

In response to the numerous job cuts, California Governor Gavin Newsom in June unveiled a tool to track AI's impact on the workforce . "As AI advances, we aren't just watching from the sidelines; we're reimagining how we prepare California through strong governance and innovative policy." And recently, more than 4,500 Google workers signed a petition calling for layoff protections as things get worse. Some of the protections they're asking for include buyouts before mandatory layoffs and guaranteed severance.

TrueUp finds that layoffs seem to be moving at a faster rate than last year — over 245,000 workers in tech were let go in 2025, while there have been more than 185,000 layoffs in 2026 so far. Several of the companies below have laid off employees due to increased spending in AI. We'll get into the reasons for the layoffs.

Oracle employees were impacted by yet another round of layoffs in September. The total number of employees laid off this time around is not currently known. The tech giant reportedly set employees early morning emails on Monday, September 14, letting those affected know it would be their last working day. It's also reported that, with these layoffs, Oracle is looking to offset the amount of money is pouring into AI chips and data centers. Earlier this year, Oracle laid off 21,000 people.

Uber announced it will cut 3,300 jobs, or about 10% of its workforce, in a big restructuring effort. "We are removing layers, simplifying team structures, refining our global location strategy, and focusing our people and investments against the biggest opportunities ahead of us," CEO Dara Khosrowshahi said in a statement . While the cuts apply to both regular employees and managers, the company stated it will reduce the "number of employees who sit 7+ layers from the CEO" by 20%, and it will cut the number of "micro-teams" by almost 50%. The CEO's memo did not mention AI as catalyst for the layoffs, but it did explain that this restructuring will allow Uber to bring its services to more people, invest in more drivers and merchants and "build the autonomous future."

According to an AppleInsider report , Apple laid off at least 60 people in its Vision Group, which is the team responsible for the Vision Pro VR headset. A Bloomberg report notes that Apple is also laying off roles in its Intelligent Systems Experience group, which is partially responsible for some of the AI systems on Apple devices. Overall, its estimated the layoffs affect more than 200 people.

When it comes to Vision Group and Vision Pro, it's been reported that incoming CEO John Ternus would be putting that product category "on ice," so this seems like the start of that process. The Vision Pro headset came out in 2024 with an eye-watering $3,699 starting price, and it remains to be seen if Apple will be pulling out of the AR/VR category entirely in the future. The Intelligence Systems changes are reportedly tied to changes that are necessary for the technical architecture for Apple's newly AI-infused Siri.

The New York Times reported that TikTok will lay off 250 people and close its Nashville, Tennessee office in October. This location was home to, in part, some of TikTok's content moderation team, although the company has not specified the reason for the layoffs or which teams they primarily affect. "We have decided to close our Nashville office to streamline our operations and better align our teams for long-term growth," a press officer for what is known as the TikTok U.S.D.S. Joint Venture said in a statement to the Times.

Zillow will lay off just over 500 people as it enacts organizational changes across the company. "These are difficult decisions that reflect both the strides we're making in our strategy and the reality of what is required of us to grow at scale," CEO Jeremy Wacksman wrote in a press release . Wacksman didn't go into detail about what organizational changes were made, or which departments are bearing the brunt of the layoffs. "These changes are about ensuring we have a disciplined cost structure and getting more efficient, with the right people in the right positions," he wrote.

Etsy laid off about 220 people, or 12% of its workforce, as it attempts to simplify its organizational structure. The cuts primarily affected the product and engineering teams, and Etsy CEO Kruti Patel Goyal said that the layoffs were necessary to build "the organization we believe Etsy needs for the future." An Etsy spokesperson told CNBC that the cuts were not driven by artificial intelligence adoption.

Microsoft has begun another round of layoffs that affects 4,800 jobs , or around 2.1% of its workforce. The Xbox division is getting hit the hardest, with 3,200 roles getting cut through fiscal year 2027, Xbox chief Asha Sharma said in a post on X — 1,600 people were let go on July 6. Shortly after those layoffs were revealed, it was announced that Sharma was appointed to a U.S. Federal Reserve task force to help advise it on "productivity and jobs." Other appointees include Marc Andreessen of Andreessen Horowitz and Charles I. Jones, professor of economics at Stanford University.

Intel is reportedly downsizing its data center group, despite strong performance. The company hasn't disclosed how many roles would be affected.

Visa will be cutting about 2,600 jobs, which amounts to about 7% of its workforce. The layoffs will primarily affect the technology and product teams, and the impetus in part is to make the company more efficient. "To capture the opportunities ahead and best position Visa to lead this transformation, we must continue evolving how we work," Chief Executive Officer Ryan McInerney wrote in a memo. "AI is also helping to accelerate this evolution and shape the way work gets done at Visa." But according to Bloomberg's report, AI was not the only factor to influence Visa's decision to do these layoffs. The company reportedly intends to reinvest in things like consumer payments and value-added services like stablecoin.

Software company Monday.com will be laying off 20% of its workforce, which comes out to about 630 people. This comes as the company makes a pivot to AI and is attempting to make its AI platform a core offering of its business. Earlier this year, it designed its main product around the idea that business customers increasingly want its employees to work with AI agents.

Patreon laid off 20% of its workforce, or 93 people, as a result of the company "changing our organizational structure and how we work." But Patreon was explicit in its email to creators and staff that "we are not making the above changes because we believe AI replaces humans." However, the email also said "AI has fundamentally transformed the tech industry, though, including how we work."

Uber has reportedly laid off 10% of its customer service division, according to a Bloomberg report, as it looks to "embrace artificial intelligence" and simplify its ranks. The company also stated in May that it would slow hiring as it makes use of AI more internally.

Samsung is eliminating 179 jobs as it moves its New Jersey headquarters to Texas later this year. The move is expected to impact around 1,000 workers. We're now getting a fuller picture of what that looks like: according to Reuters , 739 roles at Samsung's New Jersey location have been affected in some way. Some have been offered relocation packages as the company shifts its headquarters to Texas, while others have been let go. In addition, it's reported that 100 roles in its Texas location, primarily in the mobile division, have also been let go.

Amazon will lay off some people in its artificial general intelligence group, although the company has not disclosed how many roles will be affected. "This is a fast-moving space, and we're sharpening our focus on the initiatives that matter most for customers, so we can move faster on what counts," an Amazon spokesperson told CNBC.

Sony Interactive Entertainment released a statement that it's cutting "a significant number of employees" from its Bungie workforce. That includes most of the Destiny team and some Marathon team members, as well as SIE teams that support Bungie's operations. The email didn't say how many employees were affected.

Electric vehicle maker Lucid announced it's cutting around 18% of its workforce, and also noted COO Marc Winterhoff's leaving the company, Reuters reported . The layoffs are in an effort to "​boost profitability amid growing competition." The cuts affect full-time employees, contractors and hourly manufacturing workers.

Cloud computing services company Rackspace laid off 750 workers , or around 15% of its workforce. The cuts are driven by a shift in focus toward AI.

EV company Rivian let go of hundreds of employees , which amounts to around 2% of the company's workforce, the Wall Street Journal reported . Those affected were part of Rivian's service and customer organization, which handled marketing and sales.

Trading platform company Robinhood is planning to lay off 10% of its staff to restructure, the Robinhood Comms account shared on X today — that's around 290 jobs. It's unclear if the layoffs are AI-related, but CEO Vlad Tenev noted the company will be "utilizing frontier technologies to push our execution even further."

Salesforce laid off at least 86 employees in California, though Business Insider sources say job cuts also occurred in Washington and outside the U.S. as well. The cuts reportedly affect employees involved with Salesforce's Agentforce AI product, Mulesoft IT integration tool and its Marketing Cloud software.

Groupon is planning to lay off roughly 25% of its workforce , which will result in 400 job cuts. Those positions are expected to be eliminated by the end of the third quarter. This is in an effort to restructure the company and rebuild it as an AI-native company.

In another set of AI-related layoffs, website builder Wix said it was cutting around 20% of staff. Wix cofounder and CEO Avishai Abrahami announced the cuts on X , pointing to the changes AI is bringing to the industry and stating "we need to become a faster, leaner, and flatter organization." He also put part of the blame on the Israeli Shekel to U.S. Dollar exchange rates, which impact the company because it's based in Israel. The cuts are expected to impact around 1,000 roles, based on Wix's headcount.

Webflow, a website builder and hosting company, conducted a round of layoffs that an employee called "a bloodbath" in a statement to the San Francisco Chronicle . It's unclear how many employees were impacted, but one anonymous developer from the company told the Chronicle they believe it was larger than Webflow's last major round of layoffs, which affected 8% of its workforce in 2024. As with other recent layoffs, it looks like a shift to AI is to blame here. "AI is rewriting the rules for how marketing teams create, test, and optimize digital experiences," CEO Linda Tong said in a statement . "And the companies that move decisively through moments like this are the ones that come out ahead."

ClickUp CEO Zeb Evans announced that the company cut 22% of its workforce as it turns toward AI to improve productivity. He claimed it "wasn't about cutting costs," but about funneling savings from the cuts "directly back into the people who stay." The company has introduced million-dollar salary bands reserved for employees who "create outsized impact using AI."

Intuit is planning to lay off 3,000 employees, or about 17% of its workforce, Reuters reports . CEO Sasan Goodarzi sent a memo to employees noting the layoffs would help the company's efforts of focusing on infusing AI across its services.

Meta has officially begun cutting 10% of its workforce , totaling around 8,000 employees. In addition, it plans to close 6,000 open roles. The reason is to allow more room for AI spending.

Like Microsoft, NPR is offering voluntary buyouts to 300 employees in the newsroom, but only 30 will be accepted. However, if the news organization doesn't receive its target number, it will result in targeted layoffs. The reason is due to the loss of federal funding.

The online retail giant cut more jobs this month, this time from the Selling Partner Services organization. These new layoffs come after Amazon cut roughly 30,000 jobs in rounds across October and January. A spokesperson told Business Insider that the most recent layoffs have affected a "small number" of employees. The Selling Partner Services team works with third-party merchants on Amazon, providing onboarding, logistics and account management support.

Cisco is cutting just under 4,000 jobs in Q4, CEO Chuck Robbins said in a blog post . Impacted employees will receive pro-rated payment of 2026 bonuses and will also receive "support in finding new opportunities" via Cisco's placement services. In June, it was confirmed that the layoffs include 471 workers in the Bay Area .

"While we are reducing roles in some areas, we are making clear, strategic investments — particularly in silicon, optics, security, and in our employees' use of AI across the company," Robbins said.

LinkedIn is planning to lay off 5% of its staff, which is around 875 employees, Reuters reports . An anonymous person told Reuters the reason is to reorganize teams and focus employees on areas ⁠where its business is growing. However, one of the sources said the reason was "not for artificial intelligence to replace jobs at LinkedIn."

GM is letting go of around 500 to 600 employees in the Information Technology sector, Bloomberg reports . The reason is to "trim costs and clear the way to bring in staff with skills in other technology areas."

Due to restructuring driven by AI, Cloudflare is cutting more than 1,100 employees . "Today's actions are not a cost-cutting exercise or an assessment of individuals' performance; They are about Cloudflare defining how a world-class, high-growth company operates and creates value in the agentic AI era," Prince and President Michelle Zatlyn said in an email to employees .

PayPal is planning to cut around 20% of its staff — nearly 4,800 employees — over the next few years, according to the Wall Street Journal . "First, we will remove duplication and layers from our organizational structure. Second, we will accelerate our AI adoption and automation across our operations," CEO Enrique Lores said to investors.

Cryptocurrency platform Coinbase is laying off 700 employees , which amounts to around 14% of its staff. CEO Brian Armstrong cites the current market and AI changing the way they work as reasons for the layoffs.

Microsoft is offering a first-ever buyout to up to 7% of its employees, CNBC reports . It's a one-time retirement program that's available for workers at the senior director level and below whose years of employment and age are 70 or higher.

Nike announced it's laying off 1,400 people this week. "Collectively, these changes will result in a reduction of approximately 1,400 roles in global operations, with the majority in technology," COO Venkatesh Alagirisamy said. "These reductions are very hard for the teammates directly affected and for the teams around them, too."

Amazon is planning to temporarily close a warehouse in Homestead, Florida, which will eliminate more than 600 jobs, Newsweek reports . The job cuts will start in July and continue through September but the giant company is giving employees the option to relocate to other facilities. The warehouse has only been open for just under two years but Amazon is already looking to update the site.

Battery recycling company Redwood Materials laid off 10% of its employees, totaling 135 people, TechCrunch reports . Those who were let go received an email from the chief HR officer telling them the layoffs were made "to sharpen our focus, our work and the size of our teams to support the direction Redwood is going in the future."

Snap is laying off 1,000 workers , which is 16% of its staff, Variety reports . The Snapchat parent company made the announcement just weeks after Irenic Capital Management asked the company to make changes to improve performance and revenue.

Snap is using AI to streamline operations and assist the now smaller workforce. "We have already witnessed small squads leveraging AI tools to drive meaningful progress across several important initiatives," Snap CEO Evan Spiegel said.

Just two months after taking over as CEO of Disney, Josh D'Amaro announced the company is laying off 1,000 of its employees, AP News reports . In addition, Marvel let 8% of its staff go after the call was made.

"Over the past several months, we have looked at ways in which we can streamline our operations in various parts of the company to ensure we deliver the world-class creativity and innovation our fans value and expect from Disney," D'Amaro said in a memo to employees. "Given the fast-moving pace of our industries, this requires us to constantly assess how to foster a more agile and technologically-enabled workforce to meet tomorrow's needs."

The wearable camera maker this year will eliminate 145 employees due to a restructuring plan to cut costs, the Wall Street Journal reported . The cuts are expected to last until the end of the year.

Vimeo is going through its third round of layoffs since it was acquired by Bending Spoons. This time, the company let go of more than 120 people, which is about 25% of its city staff .

It's been reported that 200 Meta employees in the Bay Area will lose their jobs at the end of May. That includes 124 employees in Burlingame and 74 in Sunnyvale. The company last laid off workers just a few weeks ago.

Oracle has begun implementing a big cull of its employee base . On the final day of March, more than a dozen Oracle employees announced on LinkedIn they had been let go from their jobs, Business Insider reports . It's unclear at this time how many workers were affected, but it was projected to be thousands at the start of this month.

Those laid off received the same email : "After careful consideration of Oracle's current business needs, we have made the decision to eliminate your role as part of a broader organizational change."

The job cuts are reportedly to help Oracle stem a cash drain related its expenditures on AI infrastructure. In June, Oracle revealed that it had laid off 21,000 people as part of the cuts.

Deux Ex studio Eidos-Montréal announced on March 30 that it's laying off 124 people . In response, the studio head David Anfossi has decided to leave the company.

The cuts are a result of "changing project needs and impacts across production and support teams," the gaming company said in a LinkedIn post . It also noted that the decision to lay off these employees is not related to their talent or performance.

After already having layoffs in January , T-Mobile has cut even more of its workers, GeekWire reports . It's unclear how many people were laid off at this time, but it could be in the hundreds.

"To move even faster in a dynamic market while continuing to deliver best-in-class digital experiences for our customers, we're further aligning our IT organization to support future growth and innovation… This includes the difficult decision of eliminating some roles while continuing to invest and hire in areas," T-Mobile told GeekWire in a statement.

Meta began laying off hundreds of employees on March 25, totaling around 700 people, per The New York Times . Those impacted were part of the Reality Labs team, as well as social media and recruiting teams. Though still significant, this is a much smaller number compared to a Reuters report that suggested 20% off staff would be affected by layoffs due to the increased spending on AI.

This change comes as the company is shifting away from its metaverse creation, which includes Horizon Worlds for its Quest VR headset that's operated by the Reality Labs team.

The gaming giant on March 24 announced it was laying off more than 1,000 workers in an effort to right-size the staff of its popular free-to-play online shooter, Fortnite. CEO Tim Sweeney sent a note to his staff, citing the reason for the layoffs is due to the "downturn in Fortnite engagement," which means "we're spending significantly more than we're making, and we have to make major cuts to keep the company funded." He made it a point to note the layoffs are not related to AI.

105 employees from the Red Storm Entertainment team were laid off by Ubisoft in an effort to cut costs, IGN reports . Game development has ended at the studio, so the downsizing will remain permanent. The company employed 180 people in 2022 but has seen multiple layoffs over the years.

Roughly 1,600 employees were laid off at Atlassian on March 16, which is around 10% of total workers. Ahead of the layoffs, Atlassian CEO Mike Cannon-Brookes shared a message with the entire team, letting them know the reason is to "self-fund further investment in AI and enterprise sales, while strengthening our financial profile. We're also changing the way we work and reorganising around our System of Work to move faster." Impacted employees received an email shortly after this message went out.

articles.summary: Lucknow police arrest wife, her alleged lover and aide for husband’s murder; body was boxed and dumped under a canal bridge, CCTV trail helped solve case.
articles.body: LUCKNOW: Mohanlalganj police on Friday arrested a woman, her alleged lover and his aide for allegedly murdering her husband, concealing his body in a wooden box and dumping it under a canal bridge to destroy evidence.A 16-year-old boy, reportedly the woman’s son, has been taken into police protection, officers said.The accused were identified as Sufia Bano (35), her alleged lover Munna alias Muchhad (52) and Mohammad Iqbal alias Wasir Ahmed (40). Police said they have recovered the knife allegedly used in the murder and the e-rickshaw used to transport the body.The case came to light after Kavita Devi, the first wife of Ramkishore Valmiki, filed a complaint alleging he had been killed by Sufia and her associates. Ramkishore, the police said, had been in a relationship with Sufia for around four years and married her about two years ago.Investigators said tensions escalated when Ramkishore allegedly learnt about Sufia’s relationship with Munna, leading to frequent disputes. Police also said Sufia was upset over Ramkishore’s renewed contact with his first wife and the financial support he allegedly provided to her.According to the police version, the trio planned to kill Ramkishore. On the night of Sept 14-15, Sufia allegedly left the door unlatched, enabling Munna and Iqbal to enter the house. The two men allegedly stabbed Ramkishore to death while he was asleep.After the killing, police said, the accused cleaned the scene, concealed bloodstained articles and stuffed the body into a wooden box, which was kept under a bed. The teenager was later called to assist, investigators added.On the following night, the box was loaded onto an e-rickshaw and taken to Bhavakheda canal bridge in Kankaha, where it was dumped under the bridge.To crack the case, police tracked the e-rickshaw’s movement and reviewed footage from nearly 180 CCTV cameras on the suspected route. ADCP South Vasant Kumar said technical surveillance, fieldwork and local intelligence led to the arrests. articles.title: HC raps Bengal govt for detaining Murshidabad man on mere suspicion he was Bangladeshi
articles.summary: Calcutta High Court questions Bengal govt over Murshidabad man’s month-long detention as suspected Bangladeshi; orders arrest memo and reports before Oct 8.
articles.body: KOLKATA: The Calcutta High Court on Thursday pulled up Bengal govt for detaining a Murshidabad resident for more than a month without providing him any reason why he was suspected of being a Bangladeshi.“In 1970s and ’80s, thousands of people crossed the border. Now what will you do? Will you initiate proceedings against everybody in this fashion, violating human rights?” Justice Saugata Bhattacharyya asked the state’s counsel.Sahidul Sheikh, a resident of Dubapara village, was picked up by Raninagar police on Aug 8 and has since been in the custody of the Foreigners Regional Registration Officer (FRRO).The court ordered the state to hand over Sahidul’s ‘detention/arrest memo’ to his counsel by Saturday and directed Raninagar Police Station officer in charge to file an affidavit within a fortnight stating the basis of his detention. The Murshidabad SP, who also serves as FRRO, was directed to file a report within 10 days disclosing steps taken by the state. The case will be heard again on Oct 8.Sahidul’s wife, Dejina Bibi, had moved Calcutta High Court alleging that her husband was illegally detained by police for being a Bangladeshi. Their counsel told the court that Sahidul is an Indian citizen and his name was verified and listed in SIR 2026. He has a valid voter card, PAN card and Aadhaar card.“If I am a Bangladeshi national, there’s the Foreigners Act. If I am being detained for some reason, I have to be given a memo of detention. But nothing has been given. How was it presumed that I am a Bangladeshi?” counsel Robiul Islam argued, adding that the couple have a daughter who is taking her HS exam this year.The state’s counsel, Raj Mohan Chattoraj, submitted that Sahidul had admitted to being a Bangladeshi who entered India several years ago, claimed to be the son of a deceased local resident, acquired “genuine-looking” Indian documents and surreptitiously got included in SIR 2026, which is being investigated.Justice Bhattacharyya pointed out it was unclear whether Sahidul had admitted these before cops or the FRRO. “How long will this verification process continue? It has not been detected when he crossed the border. Many people crossed it in the 70s. How can this person be detained for such a long time?” the judge asked.Justice Bhattacharyya also queried on what basis Sahidul’s credentials were deemed invalid. On the alleged fraudulent inclusion in SIR, the judge said, “Then, you need to initiate proceedings against the officer… A person has been detained from Aug 8 and we are in mid-Sept, and a document cannot be handed over?...Will the person be detained without being given any reason?”The state’s counsel submitted that Sahidul was picked up based on inputs from FRRO. “Raninagar police station is not going around picking up people. The memo describes how it is done. Bengal police officers are not going around randomly picking people up. It doesn’t happen like that,” he said. articles.standfirst: Decisão do TJMG autorizou os shows de alguns artistas na 40° Festa da Banana, em Santa Bárbara do Tugúrio, mas manteve suspensos novos pagamentos referentes à contratação de Ana Castela.
articles.summary: Decisão do TJMG autorizou os shows de alguns artistas na 40° Festa da Banana, em Santa Bárbara do Tugúrio, mas manteve suspensos pagamentos para a contratação de Ana Castela
articles.body:
Justiça autoriza show de Gustavo Mioto na 40ª Festa da Banana — Foto: Érico Andrade/g1

O Tribunal de Justiça de Minas Gerais (TJMG) autorizou a realização de alguns shows na 40ª Festa da Banana, em Santa Bárbara do Tugúrio , na região do Campo das Vertentes. Contudo, a apresentação da cantora Ana Castela, que havia sido contratada por R$ 900 mil, continua suspensa .

Por meio das redes sociais, a Prefeitura do município confirmou que o evento acontecerá entre os dias 23 e 27 de setembro. Com a nova decisão da Justiça, os shows de Gustavo Mioto, Muriel Alves, Igor Ferrari, Yuri e Troy e Delino Marçal estão autorizados , desde que não sejam realizados novos pagamentos aos artistas.

A determinação, contudo, manteve a proibição do show de Ana Castela, que havia sido contratado por R$ 900 mil .

Segundo o relator, mesmo que a contratação tenha sido de forma regular, ainda é necessário avaliar a proporção da destinação de recursos públicos para as apresentações artísticas, considerando a realidade financeira do município, que tem pouco mais de 4 mil habitantes .

O magistrado também manteve a decisão que impede a Prefeitura de realizar novos pagamentos para custear as apresentações artísticas contratadas para o evento. Em caso de descumprimento, a determinação prevê multa.

Em 1º de setembro, a 1ª Vara Cível da Comarca de Barbacena determinou a suspensão dos gastos públicos destinados às

apresentações artísticas contratadas para a 40ª Festa da Banana . A decisão atendeu um pedido do Ministério Público de Minas Gerais (MPMG).

A ação foi proposta pela Promotoria de Justiça de Defesa do Patrimônio Público de Barbacena , que apontou indícios de desproporcionalidade entre os valores previstos para a contratação dos cantores e a realidade financeira de Santa Bárbara do Tugúrio.

articles.title: Morte de bebê em Santos: mãe pede justiça e pai segue foragido | G1
articles.standfirst: João Pedro Santos Alves é investigado por homicídio qualificado pela morte da filha de 4 meses. Mãe diz que vai buscar responsabilização do ex-namorado.
articles.summary: Investigado pela morte de bebê em Santos, João Pedro Santos Alves segue foragido enquanto a mãe da criança pede justiça por homicídio qualificado.
articles.body:
"Ele tirou tudo de mim" , diz Alicia Garcez sobre o ex-namorado foragido pela Justiça pela morte da filha do casal em Santos , no litoral de São Paulo. João Pedro Santos Alves é investigado por homicídio qualificado contra a menina, que tinha apenas quatro meses.

A bebê morreu no último dia 25 de agosto, dois dias após ser internada na Santa Casa de Santos. Ela apresentava hemorragia subaracnóidea (HSA) -- um sangramento na região entre o cérebro e a membrana que o reveste --, fratura no crânio e hematomas em outras regiões do corpo. O registro policial apontou que as marcas eram anteriores ao episódio que motivou a internação.

Mãe de bebê de quatro meses pede justiça pela filha. — Foto: TV Tribuna e Reprodução

Ao g1 , Alicia Garcez, de 20 anos, afirmou que fará o possível para que João Pedro seja responsabilizado pela morte da filha.

"Quero justiça. Vou fazer de tudo para que ele pague pelo que fez. Ele tirou tudo de mim, sabe? As primeiras palavras, risadas, passos, tudo", disse.

Ela acrescentou que não considera nenhuma punição ao homem como suficiente para compensar a perda da filha. Apesar disso, a mulher espera que todas as medidas possíveis sejam tomadas. "Acho que nada que acontecer com ele vai ser equivalente, mas quero que seja feito tudo o possível."

João Pedro Santos Alves foi denunciado pelo Ministério Público de São Paulo pela morte da filha de quatro meses. — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal

Em nota, o escritório Ochsendorf, Campos & Cabrera Advogados, que representa João Pedro, informou que aguarda a complementação do laudo pericial e realiza uma análise detalhada dos elementos técnicos do caso.

Segundo a defesa, os elementos do processo demonstrarão que a morte da bebê foi resultado de um acidente e que não houve intenção de João Pedro de matar a filha.

Ainda de acordo com os advogados, os aspectos técnicos e circunstanciais serão esclarecidos ao longo do processo, quando, segundo eles, a dinâmica dos fatos será demonstrada.

A bebê foi levada à Santa Casa em 23 de agosto, com fratura no crânio, hemorragia subaracnóidea e hematomas pelo corpo. No primeiro depoimento, ainda no hospital, os pais disseram que ela havia caído de um carrinho.

Na delegacia, porém, o pai mudou a versão e afirmou que a menina havia caído do colo dele e que, ao tentar segurá-la, acabou empurrando a criança contra o chão. Ele era o único familiar responsável pela bebê no momento em que ela se feriu.

À época dos fatos, o g1 noticiou que o homem chegou a ser detido, mas acabou liberado em audiência de custódia. A Justiça recebeu a denúncia do MP-SP na última terça-feira (15) e decretou a prisão preventiva.

articles.title: Conheça o hotel de SC que ganhou duas chaves Michelin | G1
articles.standfirst: O Awasi Santa Catarina, em Governador Celso Ramos, foi elevado à categoria de duas chaves Michelin pelo Guia Michelin, seleção global que elenca as melhores hospedagens do mundo.
articles.summary: O Awasi Santa Catarina conquistou duas chaves Michelin. Conheça o hotel de luxo em Governador Celso Ramos que oferece villas privativas e experiências exclusivas.
articles.body:
O hotel Awasi Santa Catarina, em Governador Celso Ramos , na Grande Florianópolis , foi elevado à categoria de duas chaves Michelin pelo Guia Michelin, seleção global que elenca as melhores hospedagens do mundo.

O hotel fica em uma península particular e isolada na Costa Esmeralda, protegida por uma baía tranquila a cerca de 55 km de Florianópolis. Para chegar ao refúgio, muitos hóspedes utilizam helicópteros.

O espaço já hospedou astros internacionais como Beyoncé , Paul McCartney e Katy Perry , mas propõe uma experiência de estrela para cada cliente — desde que esteja disposto a pagar diárias a partir de US$ 2.139 (cerca de R$ 11 mil).

Diferente dos cenários de grandes resorts do Brasil, não há arranha-céus modernos ao estilo de Copacabana neste trecho do litoral. O espaço conta com apenas 25 bangalôs privativos, as chamadas villas, espalhados pela paisagem natural.

🔑🔑 Anteriormente conhecido como Ponta dos Ganchos Exclusive Resort, o estabelecimento já havia conquistado uma chave na primeira edição do guia , publicada no ano passado. Agora, passou a integrar a seleta lista dos apenas três hotéis brasileiros com duas chaves.

Villas no Hotel Awasi Santa Catarina, em Governador Celso Ramos (SC) — Foto: Divulgação

Aula de ioga, veículo 4x4 e guia particular

Ao todo, são seis categorias de villas, com áreas que variam de 80 m² a 300 m². As acomodações podem incluir sauna, piscina privativa e sala de estar.

Cada villa oferece um guia particular e um veículo 4x4. Os hóspedes podem usar o automóvel para explorar praias e trilhas da região no próprio ritmo.

Todas as acomodações contam com ventilação cruzada, painéis solares e telhados verdes, além de construção com madeira de reflorestamento.

Uma das opções é a Villa Costa Esmeralda, com diária de quase R$ 16 mil. A acomodação integra quarto e sala em um ambiente único, separado da área externa por grandes portas de vidro. O espaço também conta com sauna seca, lareira, banheiro com estrutura de spa e banheira de hidromassagem com vista para o mar.

O hotel é descrito como um espaço para relaxar. E, para isso, não faltam opções: há salas para terapias individuais ou de casal, área com três banheiras de imersão e massagens em tatame. Também são oferecidas aulas particulares de ioga ou sessões de meditação.

Também há um ateliê de alquimia, onde o hóspede pode escolher intenções, aromas e texturas para compor esfoliantes corporais, máscaras de argila, óleos bifásicos e outros tratamentos personalizados.

Hotel Awasi Santa Catarina, em Governador Celso Ramos (SC) — Foto: Divulgação

A seleção do Guia Michelin é baseada em cinco critérios universais. A avaliação atribui chaves que consideram a experiência geral de hospitalidade e os serviços individuais oferecidos aos hóspedes.

Conhecido mundialmente pelas estrelas concedidas a restaurantes, o Guia Michelin lançou a classificação voltada para a hotelaria em 2025.

O sistema de chaves segue a mesma lógica das estrelas de restaurantes: quanto mais chaves o estabelecimento recebe, maior é o reconhecimento . A classificação máxima é de três chaves.

articles.title: James Baldwin arrived in France with $40 in 1948, then spent his final 16 years in an 18th-century home he bought piece by piece
articles.summary: Europe News: When James Baldwin arrived in Paris on November 11, 1948, he was 24 years old and had just $40 in his pocket. He had left the United States amid the r.
articles.body: When James Baldwin arrived in Paris on November 11, 1948, he was 24 years old and had just $40 in his pocket. He had left the United States amid the racism and homophobia that had shaped much of his early life, hoping to find enough distance to write and understand the country he had left behind. France would remain central to his life for decades, but his final home was not in Paris. In 1971, after years of living between countries and spending time in Turkey, Baldwin settled in the small Provençal village of Saint-Paul de Vence in southern France. He moved into a house belonging to Jeanne Faure, initially renting rooms before gradually buying the property piece by piece with proceeds from his publications. The house, later known as “Chez Baldwin”, became his permanent home, workplace and gathering place during the final 16 years of his life. The purchase, however, was not legally complete when Baldwin died, leaving the property at the centre of a later dispute over its ownership.Paris gave Baldwin distance from the life he had left behindBaldwin left the United States in 1948 at a time when he was struggling to find the freedom and distance he needed to write. In Paris, he became part of the city's expatriate literary community and continued developing the work that would establish him as one of the most important American writers of the 20th century. France did not erase the difficulties Baldwin carried with him. The Smithsonian's National Museum of African American History and Culture notes that the assassinations of Black leaders during the 1960s took a profound emotional toll on him. Baldwin had known Medgar Evers, Malcolm X and Martin Luther King Jr., and their deaths contributed to a period of emotional and physical strain. The museum specifically documents King's 1968 assassination as a major turning point for Baldwin. In later accounts, Baldwin described the effect of King's death on his own life and said it contributed to his decision to seek refuge in the South of France. By 1971, Baldwin had settled in Saint-Paul de Vence. The official Saint-Paul de Vence tourism site describes the village as the place where he spent the last 16 years of his life, while the Smithsonian identifies his home there as his permanent residence from 1971 until his death.He gradually turned a rented house into his own homeBaldwin's arrival in Saint-Paul de Vence was not immediately straightforward. He initially rented several rooms and had to establish himself within a community where he was not initially well known. Simone Signoret, the French actress who was a friend of Baldwin, helped him find accommodation with Jeanne Faure. Faure initially had reservations about housing a Black man, but her relationship with Baldwin developed over time. He eventually decided to acquire the property, and according to the Smithsonian, he bought the sprawling 18th-century house piece by piece using proceeds from his publications.The arrangement was more complicated than the simple description of Baldwin as the house's owner suggests. Baldwin was still in the process of purchasing the property from Faure when he died on December 1, 1987. Because the transfer had not been fully completed, the house subsequently became the subject of a legal dispute involving Faure's family and Baldwin's estate. Accounts of the dispute describe disagreements over Faure's intentions for the property and whether it should remain within her family. That distinction does not change the fact that Baldwin had spent years transforming the house into the centre of his life. It does, however, mean that describing him as having acquired complete legal ownership during his lifetime would be inaccurate.Chez Baldwin became a place for writing and recoveryThe house was far more than somewhere Baldwin lived. The Smithsonian describes it as his permanent abode and an important social centre for artists, writers, intellectuals and members of his family from Europe, Africa and the Americas. It also provided Baldwin with a setting in which he could continue writing away from the pressures of the cities where he had previously lived. His years in Saint-Paul de Vence coincided with some of his later literary work, including Just Above My Head, published in 1979, and If Beale Street Could Talk, published in 1974. The house's location also placed Baldwin close to a network of people who became important to his daily life. He developed a close relationship with the Roux family of La Colombe d'Or, the celebrated restaurant and hotel in the village, where he regularly spent time. Dr Roger Boizard became the general practitioner for Baldwin's household for nearly a decade and also a close companion. Baldwin's circle in Saint-Paul de Vence included artists and writers such as Arman, Corice Canton, Wanda and Dick van Dijk and Nicholas Delbanco. The house gradually became a place where professional relationships and friendships overlapped with ordinary daily life.The French house remained Baldwin's final refugeThe social life surrounding Chez Baldwin extended well beyond the village. The Smithsonian's documentation of the house records visits from numerous writers, musicians, actors and artists, including Josephine Baker, Nina Simone, Miles Davis, Stevie Wonder, Maya Angelou, Toni Morrison, Henry Louis Gates Jr., Yves Montand and Simone Signoret. Harry Belafonte and Sidney Poitier are also documented among Baldwin's visitors. The garden and rooms of the house provided a setting for conversations, meals, writing and artistic exchange. Baldwin's French home therefore became closely associated with the community he built around himself during his final years. Baldwin died on December 1, 1987, at the age of 63. He had spent the previous 16 years living in Saint-Paul de Vence, making the house the longest-lasting home of the final chapter of his life. Although he had worked for years to acquire it piece by piece, the legal ownership remained unresolved when he died, setting up the dispute that followed over the future of the property.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Cuba plunges into total blackout as electrical grid collapses again, US Embassy warns
articles.summary: Cuba's entire electrical grid collapsed Friday, triggering a nationwide blackout with cellphone and internet outages reported across the island.
articles.body:
Cuba experienced a total power failure due to the collapse of its electrical grid, leading to cellphone and internet outages.

The reason for the collapse is under investigation, and the timeline to restore power is unknown, with the country's electrical system remaining vulnerable to regular and unscheduled outages.

This marks the seventh national outage in Cuba this year, with the power system struggling due to fuel shortages, U.S.-imposed oil blockade, and crumbling infrastructure.

Cuba experienced a total power failure Friday, according to the U.S. Embassy in Havana.

The embassy said the failure was due to the "collapse of Cuba's electrical grid."

According to Cuban regime media, the reason for the collapse is under investigation and the timeline to restore power is unknown."

"All U.S. citizens in Cuba or planning to travel to Cuba should be aware and plan accordingly. There are reports of cellphone and internet outages," the embassy added, noting that Cuba's electrical grid is "increasingly unstable," which has led to "multiple" nationwide power outages in the last few months.

The embassy added, "The electrical system remains vulnerable, and additional regular outages have been occurring more frequently and for longer periods. Scheduled power cuts occur daily, and unscheduled outages persist throughout Cuba."

Cuba's energy ministry also posted about the power outage on social media.

The country's power system has been struggling because of fuel shortages , the U.S.-imposed oil blockade and crumbling infrastructure.

Even when there isn't a national outage, the country often endures rolling blackouts that leave millions without power.

The last national outage happened just last month, and Friday's marks the seventh this year.

articles.title: ‘Want some peace for important deal’: Ex-employee, partner sent texts to family from executive’s phone after Gurgaon murder
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: “Our mother is waiting for me to bring back something – anything to remember Yuvraj by. His clothes, his watch… or now, even his ashes,” sa.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: “Our mother is waiting for me to bring back something – anything to remember Yuvraj by. His clothes, his watch… or now, even his ashes,” said Karishma Manchanda, the older sister of Yuvraj Singh Manchanda (31), a project manager at Adani Realty, who was killed allegedly by two of his former colleagues, his body dumped in a drain in Gurgaon.While his body was found by Haryana Police on Sept 10, the family didn’t find out till Sept 16. His body had been cremated by cops in the interim. Karishma said her family has still not been given his remains. She told TOIit was only when she went to the Badshahpur police station in Gurgaon on Sept 16 that she realised her brother’s body had been found six days ago and had already been cremated.According to Delhi Police, Yuvraj was murdered by Anya Vats and Sanyam Sachdeva, his former colleagues at a real estate firm, on Sept 6.His family eventually learnt that he had died after Delhi Police apprehended Vats and Sachdeva from Uttarakhand, following which they confessed to their crime.The family alleged that Haryana Police did not follow protocol and didn’t upload Yuvraj’s photo on Zipnet — a portal used by police in different states to share information about missing or unknown dead persons.After they filed the missing complaint, the family and friends checked Zipnet every day for any information. Details of missing or unknown deceased persons are uploaded on Zipnet or CCTNS for family members to identify them. “Every hour of the day, we would check Zipnet. There was no update,” said Rajat Jain.Karishma and one of Yuvraj’s friends, Sahil, went to Badshahpur police station on Sept 16. “We saw Yuvraj’s picture. Police said he was found in a drain on Sept 10. We were shocked to hear that his body had been cremated by police on Sept 14,” Sahil said.Haryana Police, as per the info­r­mation on Zipnet, uploaded his de­tails only on Sept 16. They, however, said Zipnet was not the principal pan-India system being used for unidentified bodies and maintained the details were uploaded on CCTNS as part of the prescribed process on Sept 11. “Had the information been uploaded on Zipnet as soon as they found his body, at least we would have been able to perform his last rites and grieve,” Jain said.Karishma, meanwhile, also said she was made to wait for five hours when she went to Badshahpur poli­ce station for information about her dead brother’s belongings. After two days, the family is yet to receive anything — his ashes, clothes, a kada, his gold ring or even the postmortem report. Sahil said police told them that they had “given away” his clothes, as they were “stinking”.Suspects sent his family textsFor two days after they saw him last on Sept 6, Karishma and her parents received messages from Yuvraj Singh Manchanda’s phone telling them he was working on an “important deal” and wanted “peace”. He refused to take their calls. A message on Sept 7 said he was flying to Bengaluru for work that day, along with a photo of a ticket. The last message came a day later, asking them not to disturb him and saying that he would call two days later.Only, Yuvraj had been killed on Sept 6. The promised call never came and Yuvraj’s family hit the panic button on Sept 11, filing a missing person complaint at Delhi’s Lajpat Nagar police station.According to Delhi Police, it was Vats and Sachdeva who kept sending messages to Yuvraj’s family members and friends to keep the ruse alive and prevent them from approaching the police.Karishma recalled that when she received his messages after Sept 6, she begged him to call, show his face or even send a voice note. “My younger sister got a message saying he would call her on Sept 10. When his phone was switched off on that day, we panicked and filed a missing persons complaint,” she said.A project manager at Adani Realty, Yuvraj was described by his friends as a passionate and dedicated employee. Hours before he disappeared, he had bought a sherwani from Lajpat Nagar for his wedding, which was scheduled for Oct.“Our mother is a heart patient and our father is paralysed. Yuvraj would come back by 10pm every day to take care of them. Now, we can only hope of getting his ashes home,” Karishma said.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Iran war costs US $45.1 billion; fatalities possibly higher than 18 reported by Pentagon
articles.summary: US News: The human and material cost of America’s war with Iran is proving larger than previously disclosed, with the Pentagon telling Congress that the confli.
articles.body: The human and material cost of America’s war with Iran is proving larger than previously disclosed, with the Pentagon telling Congress that the conflict has cost $45.1 billion so far, while a Washington Post report said the number of US military fatalities may also be higher than the Pentagon’s publicly reported tally.The Pentagon told lawmakers that the war had cost $43.6 billion as of September 3, with another $1.5 billion spent on additional fuel, according to CNN, citing sources familiar with the matter. The estimate does not include the cost of repairing damaged US military bases and buildings or provide a full accounting of indirect operational costs.The latest figure is higher than the Congressional Budget Office’s estimate of $38 billion through August 1. The CBO has estimated that the war could cost the US another $2 billion to $3 billion a month for as long as fighting continues.Human toll also under scrutinySeparately, six US officials familiar with the Pentagon’s internal casualty accounting told the Washington Post that at least 22 US service members had died in the Middle East since the war began, four more than the 18 fatalities listed in the Pentagon’s public casualty database as of Friday.One official put the number at 23, saying not all of the additional deaths were directly tied to combat but involved US personnel in the region amid the ongoing hostilities. Three US contractors based in the region have also died since combat operations began, according to the report.The Pentagon declined to address questions about the discrepancy, while details surrounding the additional deaths, including the identities of those killed and when, how and where they died, remained unclear.War’s wider costsThe financial estimate also does not capture the full cost of damage to US military infrastructure. US Central Command estimated the war had cost $43.6 billion through early September, including $28 billion to replace munitions and more than $4.3 billion in lost or damaged equipment.The conflict has also put pressure on US weapons stocks and disrupted global energy markets after Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz and Houthis have control of the Bab al-Mandeb Strait. The CBO said the war could push inflation 0.5 percentage points higher in the first quarter of 2027 because of higher energy prices.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
